hypothesis: The existing strong 3074D MiniLM profile-aware selector plus frozen epoch-3 TinyBERT pair score is useful per-rule evidence, but its shared linear head cannot learn cross-rule interactions. A zero-initialized masked set-attention residual may improve final applicability prediction while preserving the exact starting baseline.
scope: One CPU training run on original assigned NLSI train split and one frozen 245-case validation split. Architecture-plus-residual-training intervention; not a pure causal decomposition and not proof of explicit rule/evidence reasoning.

feature_input.components: 3074 exact joint_and_separate MiniLM features plus frozen selected-epoch-3 TinyBERT pair score
feature_input.case_offsets: frozen representation_ablation train_offsets/dev_offsets; candidate row order checked against native source rule counts
feature_input.scaling: exact candidate augmented head training scaler: 3074 MiniLM means/scales plus one pair-score mean/scale; no refit

baseline.zero_initialization: final residual scalar layer weights and bias are zero, so epoch0 exactly matches the frozen baseline

architecture.set_block: one batch-first 2-head masked self-attention over rules in the same profile; padding keys masked
architecture.residual: shared Linear(64,1) applied to projected embedding plus attention output

optimization.objective: case-balanced binary cross entropy on final applicability labels + 0.01 * case-mean residual squared magnitude
optimization.case_weighting: each profile total loss weight 1; per-rule BCE averaged within profile
optimization.checkpoint_selection: highest 245-case validation example-macro F1 among epoch 0 baseline and epochs 1-3; ties select earliest epoch

predeclared_gate.otherwise: do not promote or launch target; preserve run as failed development experiment
